abstract.para: &suselinux; 16 modernizes &sap; workloads by consolidating system tuning into saptune and removing sapconf. For &ha;, the platform standardizes on the next-generation SAPHanaSR-angi resource agent for &hana; and mandates a static simple-mount architecture for &s4h;. These changes accelerate failover times, simplify cluster management and safeguard custom settings during upgrades.

row.entry: Dual utilities: sapconf (basic systemd tuning) and saptune (advanced profile tuning)
sapconf is fully removed: saptune is the single consolidated tuning tool
Configurations moved out of /etc. Safe saptune configure commands introduced.
Classic resource agents: SAPHanaSR (scale-up) and SAPHanaSR-ScaleOut (scale-out).
SAPHanaSR-angi (Advanced Next Generation Interface) is the sole standard.
Unified codebase with faster failover response times.
Dynamic shared file system resources mounted/unmounted at runtime via Pacemaker
Eliminates storage bottlenecks and node fencing loops.

section.title: OS tuning for &sap; workloads: moving from sapconf to saptune
section.para: In &slea; 15, &sap; operating system tuning was handled by two separate packages: sapconf, which provided basic, systemd-based tuning, and saptune which offered advanced, profile-based tuning with active monitoring and verification.

&suselinux; 16 simplifies this model by fully removing sapconf. saptune is now the single, consolidated tool for tuning the operating system for &sap; workloads and is included directly in the base &suselinux; 16 product repositories, making it universally available.
Key architectural modifications in saptune on &suselinux; 16 include:

listitem.para: Moving configuration out of /etc: To align with the &suselinux; 16 /usr/etc transition, saptune vendor default configurations have been moved away from /etc. This ensures that any subsequent package or OS updates will not silently overwrite custom parameters.

Introduction of saptune configure commands: &suselinux; 16 introduces an interactive and safe configuration editing model. Users must use commands such as saptune configure OPTION VALUE. This command performs immediate sanity checks and verification before saving, preventing unworkable tuning configurations.
Built-in safeguards: Safeguards prevent administrators from saving broken values, ensuring the stability of the kernel and memory parameters required for &hana; databases and NetWeaver.

section.title: How is &hana; High Availability managed in &suselinux; 16?
section.para: For &hana; System Replication (SR) setups, &slea; 15 supported classic resource agents: SAPHanaSR for scale-up and SAPHanaSR-ScaleOut for scale-out setups.
In &sles4sap; 16, SAPHanaSR-angi completely replaces these legacy resource agents for all new installations.
Benefits of SAPHanaSR-angi over the legacy agents include:

listitem.para: Reduced complexity: Scale-up and scale-out scenarios use the identical software package and highly similar configuration files, unifying deployment logic across the landscape.

Faster takeovers: The agent features optimized, low-latency failure detection. It triggers significantly faster database takeover times during critical events, such as file system outages, node crashes, or an unresponsive HANA database.

Resilience to administrative errors: ANGI is designed to be more robust and forgiving during manual cluster maintenance. It reduces the likelihood of false failover triggers caused by administrator missteps.

section.title: Configuring &s4h; High Availability
section.para: Legacy &slehaa; environments configured shared file systems, such as NFS or EFS mounts for the ABAP Central Services (ASCS) and Enqueue Replication Server (ERS), as individual Pacemaker cluster resources. Pacemaker mounted and unmounted these file systems dynamically during failovers, a model that frequently caused storage bottlenecks, hung mount points and node fencing loops.
In &sles4sap; 16, the simple-mount file system structure is mandatory for all new &s4h; high availability deployments.

section.title: What is the simple mount architecture?
section.para: Instead of Pacemaker controlling NFS/EFS resources at runtime, file systems are statically mounted on all cluster nodes at boot time via systemd (configured in /etc/fstab). Pacemaker no longer manages file system mounting. It only manages the start, stop, and monitoring of SAP service instances using the lightweight SAPStartSrv resource agent, leading to highly robust and stable failover behavior.
